messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@helixmed.com>, Tom Baker <tbaker@helixmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:14:00+02:00
Subject: Decision framework & open test requests

Thanks again for your time this morning — great discussion. Quick recap and the three immediate asks so we can run a tight comparison across vendors and get legal/procurement moving.

Key pain points we captured:
- Intermittent latency spikes during peak scheduling windows (affects clinician UX and throughput).
- Need for private VPC deployment and strict audit logs for regulated PHI flows.
- Cost unpredictability: finance wants stable unit economics vs. current cloud spend.

Primary goals for the next 90 days:
1) Reduce per-1k-token inference cost by ~40% (target based on current run-rate).
2) 95th percentile inference latency < 200ms for 512-token prompts at peak load.
3) SOC2-equivalent evidence and KMS/HSM key control for model keys.

Decision criteria we agreed to use (ranked): latency SLA, security/compliance fit, total cost of ownership (including reserved capacity), integration/ops effort, model output fidelity on your sample prompts.

Open tests we proposed during the call (please confirm):
A. Live latency soak: push production sample traffic at peak QPS for 2 hours (measure P50/P95/P99 and observe tail spikes).
B. Quantization/accuracy probe: run 1k canonical prompts and compare top-1 and semantic similarity to current baseline.
C. Failover/region test: simulate region outage and validate failover latency and routing.

Attachments: vendor_comparison_table.xlsx (summary vendor matrix) and redwood-test-checklist.pdf (test plan & inputs).

Asks / next steps (sequential):
- Helena/Tom: confirm you can share the 1k canonical prompts and a 24-hour token usage export by end of day Tuesday (Aug 24).
- Camila/Aditya: we will provision a short-lived test environment and send connection details by Aug 25.
- Marissa: can you confirm procurement/PO cadence and any required vendor paperwork (NDA/BAA/PO) we should prep?

I'll set a 30-min tech-deep on Aug 25 to align infra teams — propose 10:00 CEST; please confirm.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
Camila Reyes

Camila — thanks for the thorough write-up. This mirrors what we heard internally. Quick replies inline:

- Prompts + usage export: yes, we can provide the 1k canonical prompts and a 24-hour export. I’ll deliver those by EOD Tuesday (Aug 24).
- Procurement constraints: Helix requires a standard vendor security questionnaire (we attach it to purchase requests) and an internal vendor risk check that takes ~10 business days. We can start the paperwork once we have SOC2-type evidence.
- Fidelity: our clinical reviewers are most sensitive to hallucination on medication names and dosage contexts — please ensure that your accuracy probe includes these examples.

One question: do you support per-tenant model pinning (we need a stable model artifact across the trial)? Also, can we get a rough estimate of committed-capacity pricing versus on-demand for the pilot?

If it helps, Tom and I can join the Aug 25 tech-deep.

—Elena

2) Pricing: for pilots we usually offer a short reserved tranche (4–6 weeks) that gives ~30% uplift vs on-demand; for larger reserved commitments we can move toward the 40% target you quoted. I’ll have Marissa send a preliminary committed-capacity proposal by tomorrow.

- Aug 24: Helix delivers prompts + usage export.
- Aug 25 (10:00 CEST): Tech deep-dive — confirm infra, KMS keys, network (VPC peering) and access.
- Aug 26–27: Live latency soak + quantization accuracy probes.
- Aug 30: Internal review of results; decision readout week of Sep 1.

I’ve attached a short vendor comparison summary that highlights where Redwood differentiates on private deployments, predictable capacity, and observability. I also dropped the HubSpot deal (link below) so Tom/Elena can reference the purchase record.

Subject: Internal: Helix decision frame + competitor notes (HF-4892)

Internal note — please treat as internal-only. Summarizing the customer call and where to lean competitively.

Quick summary:
- Customer: Helix Medical (clinical workflows, regulated PHI), timeline is aggressive (decision early September).
- Key risks: procurement lead time (~10 business days), fidelity on medication strings, and validation vs their production sample.

Competitor quick take (from our notes + public docs):
- ObservaAI: lower headline price; lacks private VPC offering and has limited audit log granularity — risk for Helix’s compliance bar. Useful price pressure in negotiation but weak for regulated pilots.
- CloudServe: has private deployment and strong compliance pedigree, but their inference tail is demonstrably worse under sustained burst; latency spikes reported in our internal benchmarks. Good at enterprise procurement—expect longer legal cycles.

Plan / asks:
- Marissa: lead procurement thread. Push for pilot PO + short reserved tranche (4–6 weeks). Attach the pricing template and ask for Helix’s standard vendor form so we can pre-populate. Also surface the 30% pilot uplift number and the path to 40% with commit.
- Aditya: build the test harness and include a specific medication-name robustness check. Also instrument KV cache and tail-latency tracing so we can show P95/P99 stability.
- Me (Camila): I’ll own the canary plan and the demo of observability (console walkthrough). I’ll also prepare a short one-pager comparing Redwood vs ObservaAI vs CloudServe for the customer readout.

Next internal sync: 08/24 09:30 CEST for handoffs (15 min). Please come with a list of any blockers.

Thanks — Camila
